page.layout: One page of running text, with a centred section number and a centred Greek title above a passage. No margin notes. Bottom right catchword, signature at bottom left.
page.running_head: Sect. I. Part. I. Cap. XXII.

main_text.p: befcit: fole magis descendente fit color cinericius : post hunc lu-teus : quarto loco rubeus : dein purpureus: post hunc ferrugi-neus : deinde ceruleus : tandem sequitur nigra & obscura nox. Rursus, antelucano tempore, post nigrum apparent hoc ordine, ceruleus, ferrugineus, rubeus, lutens, cinericius, albus: Unde Galenus ait non posse fieri ex albo nigrum, nisi fiat transitus per colores medios: quae assertio experientiae contraria est.
Hactenus color verus: apparens est, qui non inest corpori, sed videtur inesse, ob lumen externum incidens in corpus terminatum.
main_text.head: Εὐχρασις[?]
main_text.p: Hujusmodi colores observantur in pennis pavonum, & collis columbarum, in nubibus & mari, nec non in urinis (unde Medicorum periti in luce temperata urinas malunt despicere) quos apparentes duntaxat esse patet: (1) quia ijdem non semper apparent: (2) quia pro vario corporum ad corpus lucidum situ, & oculorum etiam positu mutantur: quod in veris coloribus non contingit. Vide Coeli. Rhodig. lib.17. cap.7. Coloris varij per lumen in columbarum collis repraesentati mentionem facit Lucretius, lib.2.

p.i: Qualis enim cæcis poterit color esse tenebris, Lumine qui mutatur in ipso? propterea quod Recta aut obliqua percussus luce refulget: Pluma columbarum quo pacto in solo videtur, Quasita cervices circum, collumq; coronat: Namq; alias fit, uti claro fit rubra Pyropo:

page.notes: No marginal notes on this page. The strip at the left edge is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Greek title "Εὐχρασις" is uncertain in its letters and is marked [?]. "XVIII." is written as a paragraph because it is a bare number. Verse lines are set as one stanza in italics. Printed "cæcis" and "ipso?" are uncertain at the letter level and are not marked beyond the Greek title.
